risks.note: Evolving regulations around digital lending, AI governance, cybersecurity and data privacy may increase localization requirements, compliance expectations and implementation timelines, requiring continued investment in product modernization and compliance frameworks.

Risk continues to rise as banking ecosystems become more digital, interconnected and data-intensive; financial institutions (customers) are expected to place increasing emphasis on operational resilience, security frameworks and fraud-prevention systems, requiring the Company to keep pace.

The financial technology landscape remains highly competitive, with participation from global banking technology providers, enterprise software companies, digital-first fintech players, specialized lending technology firms and AI-led emerging platforms.

Macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical developments, inflationary pressures and shifts in global interest-rate environments may impact technology spending priorities and investment cycles at customer financial institutions.

risks.risk: Pace of technology change / innovation risk
risks.note: Rapid advancements in AI, cloud computing, embedded finance and ecosystem banking models require sustained investment in innovation, talent and partnerships to remain competitive and future-ready.

one-line thesis: Nucleus delivered steady Q3 growth with improved delivery costs (70.4%), but faces a multi-year legacy migration drag and impending margin pressure from new labor codes. Management is prioritizing AI integration and new logo acquisition (7 in FY26) over immediate capital return, keeping cash reserves high for strategic pivots.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 220.03 Cr (+7.0% YoY, +3.0% QoQ); EBITDA: INR 32.72 Cr (-0.9% YoY, +41.8% QoQ), Margin ~14.9%; PAT: INR 20.70 Cr (-40.7% YoY, -21.3% QoQ) - YoY drop due to higher tax base vs prior year; Order Book: INR 656.68 Cr (-2.1% QoQ); Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash INR 971.6 Cr). One-offs: Hedge MTM loss of INR 0.37 Cr in reserves; Tax rate normalization impacted PAT YoY.
guidance: No specific numerical guidance provided (standard policy); Qualitative outlook: Migration to Neo to take 3-4 years; Delivery costs expected to rise due to labor codes; AI to be embedded, not separate revenue line.
order book & pipeline: INR 656.68 Cr total (Product: INR 588.74 Cr; Services: INR 67.94 Cr). Down from INR 671.10 Cr in Q2 due to conversion of orders to revenue.
segment / subsidiary detail: Product Revenue: INR 185.58 Cr (84.3% of mix); Projects/Services: INR 34.45 Cr. New logos (7 in FY26, 2 in Q3) are exclusively for FinnOne Neo. Legacy vs Neo customer split approx 50:50 by count.
growth verticals / optionality: MSME lending, Gold Loans, Finance Against Securities, and Co-lending modules identified as key traction areas. Geographic expansion slow in Australia; US/EU impact minimal from tariffs.
margins & cost dynamics: Delivery cost at 70.4% (improved from 73.9% QoQ). Management warns this is unsustainable; new labor codes will increase manpower costs. Marketing spend rising (7.8% of rev) to support new geographies.
capex / expansion: Minimal; INR 2.94 Cr gross addition in Q3 (mostly software INR 2.43 Cr). Asset-light model.
capital allocation: Holding significant cash (INR 971.6 Cr). No buyback or special dividend planned currently; cash reserved for AI investments and potential M&A/strategic moves in next 2-3 quarters.
risks & watch-items: Slow migration of 50% legacy base to Neo (3-4 year timeline); Margin compression from labor code changes; High cash drag on ROE if not deployed; Slow scaling in non-India geographies.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'steady performance' and 'long-term strategy'; Transparent about migration difficulties and cost headwinds; Defensive on capital return until AI strategy crystallizes.
non-obvious takeaways: While revenue grew, the order book declined QoQ, suggesting a 'consumption' phase where execution is outpacing new bookings temporarily. The 50:50 split between legacy and Neo customers represents a significant hidden operational drag not fully quantified in revenue yet.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global BFSI industry undergoing structural transformation driven by digital acceleration, AI adoption, regulatory modernization and demand for operational resilience
- Financial institutions transitioning from legacy environments to cloud-enabled, API-first, intelligence-led platforms
- Generative AI estimated by McKinsey to create between US$200 billion and US$340 billion annually in additional value for the global banking industry, driving investment in underwriting, servicing, fraud management and compliance
- Global digital lending platform market projected to grow from ~US$10.55 billion (2024) to ~US$44.49 billion by 2030 (~27.7% CAGR) per Grand View Research
- India digital lending platform market projected to grow from ~US$486.6 million (2024) to ~US$2.45 billion by 2030 (~31.5% CAGR) per Grand View Research
- India's digital financial ecosystem expanding rapidly: UPI transactions grew from ~92 crore (FY18) to 13,116 crore (FY24), with UPI now accounting for ~49% of global real-time payment volumes
- Cross-border financial services and regional expansion gathering momentum, particularly across emerging markets
- Regulatory and compliance-driven transformation (digital lending governance, data privacy, AI governance) remains a key driver of technology investment across banks and NBFCs
- MSME financing, co-lending models, embedded finance and ESG-linked lending expected to see sustained traction

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Delivery cost at 70.4% (improved from 73.9% QoQ). Management warns this is unsustainable; new labor codes will increase manpower costs. Marketing spend rising (7.8% of rev) to support new geographies.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Holding significant cash (INR 971.6 Cr). No buyback or special dividend planned currently; cash reserved for AI investments and potential M&A/strategic moves in next 2-3 quarters.

capex_expansion.body: During the year the Company incorporated a new wholly-owned subsidiary, Nucleus Software Vietnam Company Limited, based in Hanoi (incorporated February 5, 2026), which is yet to commence operations. It is intended to serve as a hub not just for Vietnam but also for future expansion into Cambodia, Laos and other Mekong region countries. Nucleus Software Ltd. (India) operates from a 17.41-acre co-developed facility in the Mahindra World Special Economic Zone, Jaipur, providing delivery capacity for larger clients. As at March 31, 2026 the Company and its subsidiaries maintain offices across India (New Delhi, Noida, Jaipur, Pune, Chennai) and overseas locations including Singapore, USA, Japan, Netherlands, Australia, South Africa and Vietnam.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'steady performance' and 'long-term strategy'; Transparent about migration difficulties and cost headwinds; Defensive on capital return until AI strategy crystallizes.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Four-decade domain expertise in enterprise lending and transaction banking software, serving more than 200 banks and financial institutions across 50+ countries
- Deep operational embeddedness with customers: lending platforms manage loan portfolios exceeding US$1.2 trillion and transaction banking platforms process over US$15 trillion in transactions annually, with more than 500,000 daily users
- API-first, extensible architecture (540+ ready APIs) enabling integration with core banking systems, fintech ecosystems and credit bureaus, supporting customer stickiness
- Global delivery footprint through wholly-owned subsidiaries across Singapore, USA, Japan, Netherlands, India, Australia, South Africa and Vietnam supporting regional customer relationships and front-end sales/support

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Slow migration of 50% legacy base to Neo (3-4 year timeline); Margin compression from labor code changes; High cash drag on ROE if not deployed; Slow scaling in non-India geographies.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: While revenue grew, the order book declined QoQ, suggesting a 'consumption' phase where execution is outpacing new bookings temporarily. The 50:50 split between legacy and Neo customers represents a significant hidden operational drag not fully quantified in revenue yet.
